children.title: Photoelectric Effect
Why does colour matter, not brightness?
children.summary: Turns up red light's intensity and sees no electrons; weak UV ejects them at once (spec below)
children.spec: Wave prediction: brighter light should eventually free electrons; the simulation shows it doesn't below threshold. Photons: each photon gives hν to one electron, all or nothing. Graph: K_max against ν is a straight line with slope h and intercept −φ₀. Intensity: more photons means more electrons, but the same K_max.

children.title: Why is there a threshold frequency?
children.summary: Lowers ν until hν < φ₀

children.title: Why is K_max = hν − φ₀?
children.summary: Spends one photon's energy on escape, keeping the rest as kinetic energy (Einstein)

children.title: Why doesn't the stopping potential depend on intensity?
children.summary: Brightens the light: more electrons, same maximum energy

children.title: Photoelectric lab
children.summary: Plots K_max against ν and reads h from the slope

children.summary: Lets an orbiting electron radiate and spiral in

children.summary: Climbs the energy ladder and sees the levels bunch up

children.title: The Nucleus
Why do all nuclei have the same density?
children.summary: Sees R = R₀A^(1/3), so the volume ∝ A (about 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³)

children.title: Why is a nucleus lighter than its parts?
children.summary: Weighs the protons and neutrons separately and compares: the mass defect is the binding energy

children.title: Why does binding energy per nucleon plateau near 8 MeV?
children.summary: Plots B/A against A and sees it flat at about 8 MeV for A = 30–170, peaking near iron

children.title: Why is the nuclear force short-range and strong?
children.summary: Compares it with the Coulomb repulsion inside the nucleus; it is the same for n–n, n–p and p–p

Why is decay random but the half-life exact?
children.summary: Rolls dice for each nucleus and watches the totals follow e^(−λt) (the rationalised text names decay types only)

children.title: Why do fission and fusion both release energy?
children.summary: Moves along the B/A curve toward iron from either side; 1 kg of uranium gives about 10¹⁴ J against 10⁷ J from coal

children.title: Why does fusion power the Sun?
children.summary: Fuses hydrogen to helium and accounts for the mass lost

children.summary: Converts between λ, T½ and mean life

children.title: Energy Bands
Why do the energy levels of atoms in a solid smear into bands?
children.summary: Brings N silicon atoms closer; each sharp level splits into N levels that merge into a band

children.title: Why does the band gap decide metal, semiconductor or insulator?
children.summary: Slides Eg: about 0 (metal), 0.2–3 eV (semiconductor), more than 3 eV (insulator), and watches how many electrons reach the conduction band

children.title: Why is carbon an insulator but Si and Ge semiconductors?
children.summary: Compares the bonding electrons in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th orbits: Eg = 5.4, 1.1 and 0.7 eV

children.title: Intrinsic & Extrinsic Semiconductors
Why does a hole move like a positive charge?
children.summary: Lets a neighbouring electron fill a vacancy, again and again: the hole drifts the opposite way to the electrons

children.title: Why does one part per million of arsenic change everything?
children.summary: Dopes 5 × 10²⁸ Si atoms m⁻³ with 1 ppm As: 5 × 10²² donors swamp the 1.5 × 10¹⁶ thermal electrons

children.title: Why is nₑnₕ = nᵢ² even after doping?
children.summary: Adds donors and watches extra electrons recombine with holes: nₕ falls to about 4.5 × 10⁹ m⁻³

children.title: Why is a doped semiconductor still neutral?
children.summary: Counts the ionised donor cores against the free electrons

children.title: n-type or p-type?
children.summary: Picks a pentavalent dopant (As, Sb, P) or a trivalent one (B, Al, In) and names the majority carrier

children.title: Carrier-concentration calculator
children.summary: Finds nₑ and nₕ from the doping level and nᵢ

children.title: p-n Junction & Diode
Why does a depletion layer form at a p-n junction?
children.summary: Lets holes and electrons diffuse across until the field of the exposed ion cores pulls back as hard as diffusion pushes (spec below)
children.spec: Join: a p-region full of holes meets an n-region full of electrons; carriers start to diffuse across. Cores: each crossing leaves behind an immobile ion core (− on the p side, + on the n side), and the depletion layer grows. Balance: the cores' field drives a drift current back; the layer stops growing when drift equals diffusion, with a barrier of about 0.7 V for Si. Bias slider: forward bias narrows the layer and current flows; reverse bias widens it and the current is only μA.

children.title: Why can't you just press a p-slab against an n-slab?
children.summary: Zooms in on two 'flat' slabs: their roughness is far larger than the 2–3 Å atomic spacing

children.title: Why does forward bias lower the barrier and reverse bias raise it?
children.summary: Adds the battery's voltage to the barrier, or takes it away, and watches the depletion layer narrow or widen

children.title: Why does a silicon diode stay off until about 0.7 V?
children.summary: Raises V and sees the current stay tiny until the barrier is overcome, then shoot up

children.title: Why is there a small reverse current, and then breakdown?
children.summary: Reverse-biases the diode: only minority carriers drift (μA) until V reaches V_br

children.title: Diode I–V plotter
children.summary: Reads the forward resistance ΔV/ΔI = 10 Ω and the reverse resistance 10⁷ Ω

children.title: Rectifiers
Why does a diode turn AC into one-way current?
children.summary: Feeds a sine wave through a diode and sees only the positive halves pass (half-wave)

children.title: Why does a full-wave rectifier double the frequency?
children.summary: Uses a centre-tap transformer and two diodes: both halves come out positive, so 50 Hz in gives 100 Hz ripple

children.title: Why does a capacitor smooth the output?
children.summary: Adds C and watches it charge at each peak and discharge slowly through R_L; a large RC keeps the output near the peak

children.title: Rectifier builder
children.summary: Switches half-wave, full-wave and filter, and changes C and R_L

children.summary: Chains a step-down transformer, rectifier and filter (the regulator stage is beyond the text)
